chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: Leaving Armstrong; Battle of Swing; school with Gene Krupa

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So why did you decide to leave finally?

Well, let's see, what happened? I think I just got tired of the road and Louie Armstrong and Bennie Goodman, John Hammond got together a battle of swing between Louie Armstrong and Benny Goodman and it was back then in the big bands, Ziggy Elman was with it, Helen Ward, Gene Krupa was in the band, Teddy Wilson playing piano, Israel Crosby on bass, Lou McGarity trombone, and so we did about 12 concerts, Battle of Swing between Louie and Benny Goodman. So a lot of the easy jumps we were

traveling by bus and a lot of times by air. Well everybody in the two bands knew each other, you know, so we had a couple of buses, Benny had his bus, Louie had his bus and sometimes we'd all ride, everybody would be up in Benny's bus, sometime almost all of Benny's band would be back there riding with Louie's bunch, talking. So one trip we had a long flight by plane, and Gene Krupa and I sat together and we were just talking, and both Gene and I were saying, 'Oh, Cozy, doggone it, I'm getting a little too old to pay these out here on kind of dues, these one nighters.' So that is when we conceived the idea of getting drum school together, and Gene says, 'Yeah, Cozy, that sounds like a good idea. When I get to New York, I'll see my lawyers, you see yours, and we'll try to get it going.' So after we were in New York about a couple of days, rested, after we got a couple of days rest after the tour, Gene calls me and says, 'Cozy my lawyers like the idea.' And then's when we start bickering, getting together and opening a school, and that's when I left Louie, when Gene and I got the school together.
